newsitem.title: UK: Four companies bid for UK TV delivery franchises.
newsitem.headline: Four companies bid for UK TV delivery franchises.

text.p: Britain's Independent Television Commission on Monday said it received four applications for local delivery franchises for Milton Keynes north of London.

Local delivery franchises are the equivalent of the cable franchises granted by the former Cable Authority and enable a range of multichannel television and telecommunications services to be provided by cable or microwave distribution.

The ITC said the four applicants for the Milton Keynes franchise include BT New Towns Cable TV Limited, a unit of British Telecommunications Plc, which proposes serving 114,000 homes by year-end 2001 and submitted a cash bid of 4.5 million pounds.
Another bid was from CableTel Bedfordshire Ltd, a unit of International CableTel Inc, which proposes to serve 101,840 homes by year-end 2001 and submitted a cash bid of 148,180 pounds.

Cable Television Ltd, owned by Telecential Communications (Canada) Ltd, a joint venture of TELUS Cable Inc and KPN Kabel UK Holding BV, proposes to serve 78,000 homes by the middle of 2001 and submitted a cash bid of 1,571,000 pounds.
Metro Communications (MK) Ltd, a unit of Metro Cable TV Ltd, proposes to serve 128,579 homes by year-end 2001 and submitted a cash bid of 1,082,888 pounds.
The ITC said the cash bids made, representing a sum to be paid annually, would supplement the percentage of qualifying revenue which the ITC has already set.
The ITC said it hopes to announce a decision in spring 1997.
Separately, the ITC said it received one application for the local delivery franchise for Lothian in Scotland.

Telewest Communications (East Lothian) Ltd, a unit of Telewest Communications Plc, proposes serving 30,000 homes in the area by the end of 2002, and submitted a cash bid of 10,000 pounds, the ITC said.
